title: Biasing Techniques
intro: An amplifier only works if every transistor is in saturation at the right current. Good biasing makes that independent of process, supply and temperature.

items: Bias with currents rather than voltages where possible: mirrors from a precise reference give a current set by the reference, not by device parameters.
A resistive divider fixes a gate voltage, but the current then depends on VTH and mobility.
Source degeneration stabilises current: a resistor in the source makes ID depend weakly on VTH.
AC-couple the signal so the bias network does not load the source.
CS stage: gate tied to a divider (R1, R2) or to a mirror via a large resistor so the signal does not leak into the bias.
CG stage: the gate bias must be a stable AC ground (large capacitor); the source gets a current source.
Source follower: biased through a mirror that sets the follower's current.
Differential pair: tail current source from a mirror; the common-mode level is set by the previous stage or by feedback.

blocks.title: Divider bias
blocks.text: VDD = 1.8 V. A divider R1 = 100 kohm (top) and R2 = 200 kohm (bottom) feeds the gate of an NMOS with source at ground. If k = 2 mA/V^2 and VTH = 0.5 V, find ID.
solution: Notice the fractional change in ID is about 2*dVTH/Vov: a 50 mV VTH shift moves Vov to 0.65 V and ID to 0.42 mA, 14 percent lower. A mirror from a stable reference does much better.
